parsed_answer.content: In Java persistence frameworks like Hibernate or JPA, mapping relationships is the process of defining how object-oriented domain models translate into relational database schemas. A One-to-One relationship implies that a single record in Table A corresponds to exactly one record in Table B, often implemented via a shared primary key or a unique foreign key constraint. One-to-Many and Many-to-One are the most common patterns; the former represents a parent-child hierarchy (e.g., a Department having many Employees), while the latter is the inverse, where the child holds the foreign key reference back to the parent. Many-to-Many relationships are more complex, requiring an intermediary join table to resolve the cardinality, as relational databases cannot natively store collections of foreign keys in a single column without violating First Normal Form.

items: In One-to-Many mappings, always use 'mappedBy' on the parent side to prevent the creation of redundant join tables and to designate the child as the owner of the relationship.

Many-to-Many relationships should be handled with caution; use a @JoinTable annotation to define the link table, and consider using a Set instead of a List to avoid Hibernate's 'MultipleBagFetchException' when fetching multiple collections.
For performance, always utilize 'FetchType.LAZY' on all relationships to avoid N+1 query problems, explicitly using JOIN FETCH in JPQL or EntityGraphs when you know you need the associated data.

Orphan removal should be enabled in One-to-Many relationships if the lifecycle of the child is strictly bound to the parent, ensuring that removing a child from the collection triggers a DELETE statement rather than just nulling the foreign key.

parsed_answer.content: A classic production trap is the 'N+1' query issue. If you map a One-to-Many relationship with EAGER fetching, Hibernate will execute one query for the parent and N additional queries for each child collection, which will cripple your database performance under load. Always default to LAZY and use fetch joins only when necessary.

title: How do you map relationships: One-to-One, One-to-Many, Many-to-One, Many-to-Many?
